name: Phishing
description: Adversaries send phishing messages with malicious attachments or links to gain access.

name: Spearphishing Attachment
description: Phishing email with a malicious file attachment designed to execute on the target.

name: Spearphishing Link
description: Phishing email containing a malicious link directing victims to credential harvesting or exploit pages.

name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
description: Exploitation of weakness in an internet-facing service or application.

name: External Remote Services
description: Abuse of external-facing remote services such as VPNs, Citrix, or RDP for initial entry.

name: Valid Accounts
description: Use of legitimate credentials to gain access, bypassing authentication controls.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
description: Abuse of command-line interpreters and scripting engines to execute commands.

name: PowerShell
description: Use of PowerShell — including encoded commands, IEX, and download cradles — to execute malicious code.

name: Windows Command Shell
description: Use of cmd.exe or batch scripts to execute commands on Windows systems.

name: Python
description: Use of the Python interpreter to execute malicious scripts or one-liners.

name: User Execution
description: Reliance on user action (double-clicking a file, visiting a URL) to trigger malicious code.

name: Windows Management Instrumentation
description: Abuse of WMI for local or remote execution of commands and scripts.

name: Scheduled Task / Job
description: Use of system job schedulers to execute malicious programs at set times or intervals.

name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
description: Configuration of system settings to launch malicious code when a user logs on or the system boots.

name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
description: Adding entries to registry run keys or startup folders to maintain persistence across reboots.

name: Create Account
description: Creating local or domain accounts to maintain persistent access.

name: Server Software Component
description: Installing malicious server-side components such as web shells to maintain access.

name: Office Application Startup
description: Abuse of Microsoft Office startup mechanisms to gain persistence.

name: Office Template Macros
description: Malicious macros embedded in Office templates that execute on document open.

name: Process Injection
description: Injecting code into running processes to execute with elevated privileges or evade detection.

name: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
description: Bypassing UAC or sudo controls to execute with elevated permissions.

name: Access Token Manipulation
description: Stealing or forging security tokens to escalate privileges or impersonate other users.

name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
description: Exploiting software vulnerabilities to gain higher-privileged execution.

name: Obfuscated Files or Information
description: Encoding, encrypting, or otherwise obfuscating files and code to avoid detection.

name: Masquerading
description: Renaming or disguising malicious files and processes to appear legitimate.

name: Indicator Removal
description: Deleting logs, files, or other artefacts to remove evidence of compromise.

name: Modify Registry
description: Modifying registry keys to hide configuration data or disable security tooling.

name: Deobfuscate / Decode Files
description: Decoding or deobfuscating files or information at runtime to evade static analysis.

name: Impair Defenses
description: Disabling or tampering with security tools, logging, or protective controls.

name: OS Credential Dumping
description: Attempting to dump credential material from the operating system or memory.

name: LSASS Memory
description: Dumping credentials from the LSASS process memory using tools such as Mimikatz.

name: Unsecured Credentials
description: Searching for credentials stored in insecure locations such as files or environment variables.

name: Credentials In Files
description: Searching for credentials stored in plaintext or weakly protected configuration files.

name: Private Keys
description: Searching for private cryptographic key material (SSH, PEM) left accessible on the filesystem.

name: Cloud Instance Metadata API
description: Querying cloud metadata endpoints (e.g., IMDS) to obtain instance credentials or keys.

name: Brute Force
description: Attempting to guess credentials through exhaustive trial of passwords or hashes.

name: System Information Discovery
description: Gathering detailed information about the target OS, hardware, and configuration.

name: File and Directory Discovery
description: Enumerating files and directories to identify sensitive data or attack paths.

name: Account Discovery
description: Enumerating user and group accounts to identify targets for escalation or lateral movement.

name: Network Share Discovery
description: Identifying accessible network shares that may contain sensitive data.

name: Network Service Discovery
description: Scanning the network to identify open ports, running services, and potential targets.

name: Process Discovery
description: Enumerating running processes to identify security tools, target applications, or pivot opportunities.

name: Remote Services
description: Use of legitimate remote services to move laterally through a network.

name: Remote Desktop Protocol
description: Lateral movement using the Windows Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP).

name: SMB / Windows Admin Shares
description: Lateral movement by authenticating to Windows administrative (admin$, C$) or IPC shares.

name: Windows Remote Management
description: Lateral movement using WinRM or PowerShell remoting.

name: Exploitation of Remote Services
description: Exploiting vulnerabilities in remote services to move laterally without valid credentials.

name: Data from Local System
description: Collecting sensitive files and data directly from the local filesystem.

name: Input Capture
description: Capturing keystrokes, clipboard content, or form data to steal credentials or information.

name: Application Layer Protocol
description: Using standard application-layer protocols (HTTP, DNS, SMTP) for C2 communication to blend in.

name: Remote Access Software
description: Use of legitimate remote access tools (Cobalt Strike, TeamViewer) as C2 infrastructure.

name: Ingress Tool Transfer
description: Transferring tools or additional payloads from an external system to the victim.

name: Protocol Tunneling
description: Encapsulating C2 traffic within another protocol (e.g., DNS-over-HTTPS) to evade detection.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
description: Exfiltrating stolen data over the same channel used for command and control.

name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
description: Exfiltrating data over a protocol not normally used for C2, such as DNS or ICMP.

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service
description: Exfiltrating data to cloud storage or SaaS services (e.g., Dropbox, GitHub) to avoid detection.

name: Data Encrypted for Impact
description: Encrypting files on victim systems to disrupt availability and extort payment (ransomware).

name: Inhibit System Recovery
description: Deleting backups and shadow copies to prevent recovery from ransomware or destructive attacks.

name: Service Stop
description: Stopping or disabling critical services to disrupt availability.
